_comment: Canon for every performance ratio quoted on the marketing site's high-traffic surfaces (homepage sections, page.tsx, layout.tsx metadata + JSON-LD). Same contract as commercial-terms.json: change this file first, then propagate. CI enforces it via tests/test_site_claims.py — a ratio on those surfaces that is not listed here fails the build. This exists because the site drifted: it carried a 65.6x figure attributed to three different repo sizes, a 63.6x typo of the same number, a 0.81s latency with no source in the repo, a '100% gold-file recall' that the public benchmark of the day contradicted (93.6% mean), and the real name of a private client whose field report the docs deliberately anonymize.

_evidence_levels.ci-gated: Recomputed and asserted on every PR. Cannot silently regress.
_evidence_levels.reproducible: Not a gate, but any reader can rerun it from a fresh clone and get the same number on the same machine. Token counts, and the ratios built on them, can shift slightly from one machine to another; where that has been measured, recall and found-rate did not move, and the source page states the spread (docs/benchmarks/public.md: for the current run, per-repo mean tokens within 0.8% between CI runners with and without AVX-512, recall, found-rate and NeuralMind's MRR identical, the embedding-rag baseline's MRR on click 0.69 against 0.60).
_evidence_levels.field-report: One repo, one developer, maintainer-measured. Reproducible in method, not in number. Must be labelled as such wherever it appears.
_evidence_levels.community: Submitted to docs/community-benchmarks.json by a named submitter. n is small; treat as directional.
_evidence_levels.pilot: Pre-registered and run exactly as its spec says, with raw data committed, but exploratory: small n, one repository, one agent and model. It sizes a confirmatory run; it is not a product claim and not a gate.
_evidence_levels.exploratory: Run like a pilot, with raw data committed, but NOT pre-registered: a follow-up chosen after seeing an earlier result. Weaker than a pilot; it says what happened on those tasks, not what to expect.
_evidence_levels.disclosure: Not a result: something the site states is NOT measured or NOT shown, kept here so the copy can't quietly drop it. Its `reproduce` names how a reader could measure it.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: 100% gold-file recall (40 of 40 queries, query-weighted), 100% on every repo, 100% found-rate, across 40 pre-registered queries on 4 pinned OSS repos
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: This is canon for the data, not copy for the site: the site must NOT headline '100% recall' (tests/test_site_claims.py rejects it). Forty queries is a small sample, every earlier run had at least one miss, and the next retrieval change can bring one back. Say '40 of 40 queries' and pair it with the larger 150-question retrieval eval, where the same build puts a gold file in the top five for 93.3% of questions and misses 10 (bench/retrieval/on-v4.12; misses listed per question). At v4.12.0 the three v4.10.0 misses (requests xfile-status-codes, click echo-util, flask xfile-dispatch-context) are found. NeuralMind's recall is now at or above the embedding-rag baseline's on every repo (96.25% mean for the baseline; flask 1.00 vs 0.85), but its MRR is still below the baseline's on flask (0.72 vs 0.74) and rich (0.83 vs 0.94) — say so wherever recall is compared. The embedding-rag baseline is the top 8 entries of NeuralMind's own vector index (a symbol's name, module and docstring, not code bodies), so its token count is a floor, not what a chunk RAG sending code would pay. Backed by bench/public/results.json, regenerated at v4.12.0 (tokenizer tiktoken o200k_base, neuralmind backend run read-only and counted with the benchmark tokenizer). tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes the mean, the per-repo range, the found-rate and the per-repo ratios from that file.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: ripgrep (query keywords, top five files opened whole) found the gold file on 32 of 40 public-benchmark queries; NeuralMind on 40 of 40
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Pair it with the 31-67x token figure wherever the site compares against grep. tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes both from bench/public/results.json.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: A gold file in the top five for 93.3% of the 150-question retrieval eval (30 pre-registered questions on each of requests, click, flask, rich and NeuralMind's own repo); 10 misses, listed per question
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: The larger sample the 40-query public benchmark is always paired with, so '40 of 40' is never read as perfect recall. The site computes the rate and the miss count from the baseline configuration in bench/retrieval/on-v4.12/results.json at build time (site/src/lib/evidence.ts), so they can't be retyped wrong; when the eval is re-run into a new directory, update this entry's source and that import together.

non_ratio_headline_claims.note: The measured replacement for '~800 tokens instead of ~50,000', which paired a rough per-question figure with the CLI's old fixed 50K-token estimate — not a measurement of anything. Quote these ranges (or the 150-question retrieval eval's ~830 tokens per question at v4.12.0, bench/retrieval/vs-v4.11) with their source. tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes both ranges from bench/public/results.json.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Synapse recall never lowers top-k hit rate, at a neutral token budget
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: The CI gate is DIRECTIONAL: test_synapse_recall_does_not_reduce_hit_rate asserts on >= off, and test_synapse_recall_is_budget_neutral bounds the reduction delta. It does not gate a magnitude. The +6.1 pts (77.2% -> 83.3%) figure published in docs/wiki/ traces to the v0.25.0 2x2 study; the self-benchmark's current Phase 2 output reports +3.5 pts (74.6% -> 78.1%). Do not quote either magnitude as 'CI-gated' — quote the gate, and let the reproduction command give the number. HISTORY: this gate measured -1.75 pts (74.6% -> 72.8%) on AVX-512 hosts and +3.5 elsewhere, bit-stably, for months. A 2-point tolerance was added 2026-08-29 to make it pass and was reverted; the cause was displacement dropping the ranked tail, which could evict a module's only representatives. Fixed 2026-08-31 by choosing displacement victims whose module another survivor still covers. Both host classes now measure +3.51 on this fixture (74.6% -> 78.1%), verified on an avx512f container and a non-avx512f CI runner at the same commit.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Faithfulness vs naive truncation at a matched token budget: CI fails if the mean delta falls below -0.10 (built-in backend, mean of 3 runs on the reference fixture). At v4.12.0 it measured +0.265 (0.839 vs 0.574 expected-fact recall) with CI's command on one machine, where v4.11.1 measured +0.027; at v4.3.4 CI measured -0.054, a loss the site published.
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Do NOT describe this as 'never worse' or 'beats truncation'. ci-benchmark.yml asserts mean_faithfulness_delta >= -0.10, not >= 0.0: the gate was relaxed because sample_project mixes code with prose chapter summaries, where a matched-budget naive baseline can edge out the built-in backend. CI output on #539: built-in recall 0.451 vs naive 0.505, delta runs [-0.054, -0.054, -0.054]. Earlier releases measured +0.013 to +0.143. v4.12.0 (L2 lists the query's other candidates, 8 L3 hits from 20 spread across files) measured +0.265 (0.839 vs 0.574) on a 4-core AVX-512 container running the ci-benchmark.yml step, where the v4.11.1 code on the same machine measured +0.027 — so the machine reads higher than #539's runner did; CI's own number for v4.12.0 is in the PR's self-benchmark run. Quote the gate and the current, dated measurement; re-check both whenever ci-benchmark.yml or the fixture changes.

Task outcomes, pilot: on 20 pre-registered bug-fix tasks, Claude Code with and without NeuralMind solved the same number of tasks at no measurable difference in cost; the agent called none of NeuralMind's MCP tools

non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Replaces the disclosure 'Task outcomes are not measured' (removed 2026-10-21, when this pilot was published). A RESULT, not a disclosure, and a null one: quote it with the same prominence as the retrieval wins, labelled 'pilot', with its interval, and never as a product claim (the spec says so). Say 'a 20-task pilot found no cost difference', with a link; never write that task outcomes are 'not measured' again, and never that NeuralMind makes agents cheaper, faster or more accurate. The finding: in the 60 neuralmind-arm runs the agent called none of the 28 MCP tools the server listed; NeuralMind reached it only through its Claude Code hooks (install-hooks), which ran in all 60. Pinned: claude-sonnet-5-5, Claude Code 2.1.287, NeuralMind 4.15.1; one repository (NeuralMind's own), cold start, cost is Claude Code's estimate at API prices. The confirmatory run follows the spec on new tasks; nothing about it may be claimed before it is run. tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes `figures` from report.txt and runs.jsonl.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Task outcomes, exploratory rerun: with the change released in v4.21.0, which tells the agent when to use NeuralMind's tools and lists six instead of 28, Claude Code on the pilot's 20 tasks still called none of them and showed no measurable difference in cost
non_ratio_headline_claims.reproduce: python -m evals.task_outcome.run --tasks evals/task_outcome/tasks.json --out <rerun> --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --seeds 3 --arms neuralmind --tool-venv <venv with neuralmind built from commit eee0a5be> --test-python <venv>/bin/python --work-dir <scratch>; then pair it with the pilot's baseline arm in a new directory and analyze that: mkdir <pair> && { grep '"arm": "baseline"' bench/task_outcome/pilot/runs.jsonl; cat <rerun>/runs.jsonl; } > <pair>/runs.jsonl && python -m evals.task_outcome.analyze <pair> (with bench/task_outcome/exploratory-agent-uptake for <rerun>, this reproduces report.txt's paired figures from the committed runs; bench/task_outcome/exploratory-agent-uptake/README.md)

Label it 'exploratory', never 'pilot' or 'confirmatory', and never quote it as evidence that NeuralMind helps or hurts: it shows that telling the agent about the tools didn't change what it did on these tasks. tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes `figures` from report.txt and runs.jsonl.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Task outcomes, Hermes pilot: on the same 20 bug-fix tasks, Hermes-Agent on a local gpt-oss:20b model solved 10 with NeuralMind's plugin and 8 without, too few tasks apart to be significant (one-sided McNemar p = 0.25), with no measurable difference in tokens per task
non_ratio_headline_claims.reproduce: python -m evals.task_outcome.run --agent hermes --tasks evals/task_outcome/tasks.json --out bench/task_outcome/hermes-pilot --model gpt-oss:20b-64k --seeds 1 --max-turns 120 --timeout 3600 --tool-venv <venv with neuralmind==4.23.1> --test-python <venv>/bin/python --work-dir <scratch>, then the same with --seeds 3 (stage 2 skips the recorded runs), then python -m evals.task_outcome.hermes_sessions bench/task_outcome/hermes-pilot && python -m evals.task_outcome.analyze bench/task_outcome/hermes-pilot
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: A separate exploratory study on the Claude Code pilot's 20 tasks, never pooled with it. Primary endpoint: tasks solved (most of a task's 3 seeds), one-sided McNemar on the tasks only one arm solved; supported only at p < 0.05, which needs at least 5 such tasks all one way. Two went to NeuralMind and none the other way, the lowest p two can give. Quote it as '10 vs 8 tasks, not significant', never as a percentage gain or a ratio of the two. NeuralMind reached the agent only through its Hermes plugin (a context block on every prompt, the session recap, edit learning); neither arm had an MCP server. Pinned: Hermes-Agent v0.22.5, gpt-oss:20b-64k on Ollama on one 16 GB GPU, NeuralMind 4.23.1; one repository (NeuralMind's own), a fresh index each run. Keep two caveats beside it: in 36 of the 120 runs a command the agent had started (33 of them pytest over the whole suite) was still running when judging began, and the verdicts stand as recorded (the spec, 2026-10-30; harness 2 now stops such commands first); and the machine's Hermes cron jobs were paused partway through, with both arms on both sides of the pause, which can move minutes. tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes `figures` from report.txt and runs.jsonl.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Task outcomes, memory track: on the same 20 tasks in a fixed order, Hermes-Agent on a local gpt-oss:20b model solved 9 with NeuralMind's learned state carried from task to task and 7 starting fresh, too few tasks apart to be significant (one-sided McNemar p = 0.3125)
non_ratio_headline_claims.reproduce: python -m evals.task_outcome.run --agent hermes --track memory --chains 3 --fresh 3 --tasks evals/task_outcome/tasks.json --out bench/task_outcome/memory-track --model gpt-oss:20b-64k --max-turns 120 --timeout 3600 --tool-venv <venv with neuralmind==4.23.1> --test-python <venv>/bin/python --work-dir <scratch>, then python -m evals.task_outcome.hermes_sessions bench/task_outcome/memory-track && python -m evals.task_outcome.analyze bench/task_outcome/memory-track
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: A separate exploratory study on the same 20 tasks, never pooled with the other two pilots. It asks whether NeuralMind's learned state (its synapse store and session recaps), carried along 3 chains through the tasks in a fixed order, helps the next task, against 3 fresh runs per task that start with nothing learned, side by side on the same days. Primary endpoint: tasks solved (most of a task's 3 runs), one-sided McNemar on the tasks only one condition solved; supported only at p < 0.05, which needs at least 5 such tasks all one way. Quote it as '9 vs 7 tasks, not significant', never as a percentage gain, a ratio, or evidence that NeuralMind learns a codebase. Keep beside it what the spec records: the fresh arm repeats the Hermes pilot's neuralmind arm, which solved 10 tasks two days earlier, and the 9 carried solved are all among those 10; the mechanism didn't move (most runs' blocks put a gold file first on 11 tasks in each condition); tokens per task rose a median 18.2% with the carried state, CI including no change. From position 17 a chain carries only the session recaps NeuralMind keeps (its newest 10, plus any from the last 24 hours), as shipped; the learned edges carry whole. The harness's check that NeuralMind ran was changed before the last 7 runs, after 10 false alarms, without changing what the agent saw (the spec, 2026-11-01). Pinned: Hermes-Agent v0.22.5, gpt-oss:20b-64k on Ollama on one 16 GB GPU, NeuralMind 4.23.1; one repository (NeuralMind's own). tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes `figures` from report.txt and runs.jsonl.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: The synapse layer's benefit on a real repository over time is not shown: the CI gate is directional, on a ~500-line fixture, and a 20-task pilot that carried NeuralMind's learned state from task to task found no significant difference
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: A disclosure, not a result. `neuralmind eval . --synapse-ab` runs a project's own gold questions with synapse recall on and off and records the difference in .neuralmind/eval_history.jsonl, with the usage-learned counts (LTP edges, transitions), so a user can see whether it grows as usage teaches the layer more. Recall also follows the call and import edges every build seeds, so a fresh build can already differ. No such history is published. The memory-track pilot (bench/task_outcome/memory-track/, 2026-11-01) carried the synapse store and session recaps through 20 tasks on NeuralMind's own repository and found 9 vs 7 tasks solved, p = 0.3125, with the block's gold-file ranking unchanged: it doesn't show the benefit either. Do not write that the layer 'compounds', 'gets smarter over time' or 'improves retrieval continuously' until one is.

_attribution_rule: A ratio is only correct together with the repo it was measured on and the evidence level it carries. The original defect was not a wrong number — 65.6 is a real measurement — it was that number bolted to a '1,486-node production codebase' that appears in no dataset. So entries that were measured on a specific repo declare `nodes`, and tests/test_site_claims.py checks the (ratio, node-count) pair and the claimed evidence level wherever the site states them, not just the numeric value.
